Transistor.Type: Through-hole transistor with a black plastic casing and three metallic leads
Transistor.Color: Black body with a circular marking containing a stylized 'T' symbol; metallic leads are silver-colored
Transistor.Size: Body approximately 10mm in height and 5mm in width / 1.5 cm in height and 0.8 cm in width; leads extend about 15mm downward / 10-12 mm in length from the body to the solder points
Transistor.Material: Body made of black plastic or epoxy resin; leads are made of metal, likely tin-plated copper or similar conductive alloy
Transistor.Composition: Plastic encapsulated semiconductor die with three metal leads for electrical connection
Transistor.Relative Location: Positioned centrally in the image, mounted on a perforated board
Transistor.Orientation: Standing upright with leads pointing downward
Transistor.Connection/Attachments: Leads are soldered into three adjacent holes on the perforated board, forming electrical connections

Copper Trace.Type: Thin, flat conductive pathways on the surface of the perforated board
Copper Trace.Color: Copper-colored, with a slightly oxidized or tarnished appearance in some areas
Copper Trace.Size: Width varies between 0.5 mm to 1 mm; length extends across the board in parallel lines
Copper Trace.Composition: Pure copper or copper alloy, used for conducting electrical current
Copper Trace.Quantity: Multiple traces visible, running vertically and horizontally across the board
Copper Trace.Relative Location: Located beneath the transistor’s leads and surrounding the holes, forming a grid pattern
Copper Trace.Orientation: Vertical and horizontal traces intersecting to form a grid
Copper Trace.Connection/Attachments: Connected to the transistor’s leads via solder joints, to the holes, and likely to other components or power rails

Perforated Board.Type: Printed circuit board (PCB) with a grid of holes for component mounting and copper traces for electrical connections
Perforated Board.Color: Copper-colored surface with dark holes and traces
Perforated Board.Size: Visible portion is rectangular, with multiple rows and columns of holes / 5x5cm
Perforated Board.Material: Copper-clad laminate material, typically FR-4 or similar composite
Perforated Board.Composition: A layered material consisting of a non-conductive substrate (e.g., fiberglass) with copper foil on both sides, etched to form traces and drilled to form holes
Perforated Board.Quantity: One perforated board visible in the image
Perforated Board.Relative Location: Occupies the entire visible area of the image, serving as the mounting surface for the transistor
Perforated Board.Orientation: Horizontal, with traces running parallel to each other
Perforated Board.Connection/Attachments: The board connects the transistor leads to the copper traces and provides a mounting platform for other components

Solder Joint.Type: Melted solder connecting the transistor leads to the copper traces or board holes
Solder Joint.Color: Metallic grayish with some darkened areas from oxidation or heat
Solder Joint.Size: 1-3mm in diameter, with a slightly irregular, bulbous shape
Solder Joint.Composition: Melted metal alloy forming a bond between lead and copper trace, or filling the hole
Solder Joint.Quantity: Three solder joints, one for each lead of the transistor
Solder Joint.Relative Location: Located at the base of each transistor lead, where it meets the copper trace or within the corresponding hole on the board
Solder Joint.Orientation: Circular, forming a small dome around the lead and trace junction, or aligned vertically, connecting the lead to the hole
Solder Joint.Connection/Attachments: Electrically connects the transistor to the copper traces, completing the circuit path, and connects the transistor lead to the copper trace and the perforated board

Hole.Type: Circular openings in the perforated board for component mounting and electrical connection
Hole.Color: Dark, appearing black or dark gray due to shadowing and oxidation
Hole.Size: Diameter approximately 2-4 mm, consistent across all visible holes
Hole.Material: Copper-clad laminate material with holes drilled through
Hole.Composition: The holes are formed by drilling or punching through the board material, exposing the copper trace beneath
Hole.Quantity: Multiple holes visible, arranged in parallel vertical columns on the board
Hole.Relative Location: Located in vertical columns, aligned with the transistor leads and copper traces, surrounding the transistor
Hole.Orientation: Circular, perpendicular to the board surface
Hole.Connection/Attachments: Each hole is connected to a copper trace and serves as the point of attachment for the transistor leads via solder joints
